summary:
We developed ASTRA-LOOP, an autonomous, offline-first bio-digital twin and clinical decision-support copilot designed for deep-space exploration. 

On long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars, communication delays of up to 22 minutes make real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible. ASTRA-LOOP addresses NASA's challenge by empowering non-physician astronauts to monitor, predict, and manage their health entirely offline. Operating through a continuous five-step closed loop (Sense, Understand, Predict, Act, Learn), the platform tracks 16+ physiological and habitat telemetry indicators across all five NASA Human Research Program hazards—including space radiation, microgravity fluid shifts, isolation, and elevated cabin CO2. 

Our system pioneers a dual-layer safety architecture that pairs rolling personal baselines (Z-scores) with strict NASA-STD-3001 and AHA absolute clinical safety thresholds, ensuring drifting baselines never mask acute disease. Through an interactive 9-organ vector human body with Hazard Lens filtering and branching clinical decision-tree wizards, crews receive tiered, actionable treatment guidance from self-care to emergency protocols. A self-calibrating N-of-1 trial engine continuously measures countermeasure efficacy to optimize personalized care.

ASTRA-LOOP is vital because it bridges the deep-space medical autonomy gap, safeguarding crew health and mission success all the way to Mars.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

ASTRA-LOOP is an autonomous, offline-first bio-digital twin and clinical decision-support copilot designed to keep astronauts healthy during long-duration deep-space missions. Built to function without Earth connectivity, it operates as a continuous five-step closed loop:

- Sense (Offline-First DTN Telemetry): Ingests 16+ physiological and environmental parameters (BP, heart rate, HRV, blood glucose, core body temperature, SpO2, cabin CO2, radiation dose, sleep, and nutrition). Telemetry buffers safely in local IndexedDB during communication blackouts.

- Understand (Dual-Layer Safety Architecture): Evaluates adaptive personal baselines (rolling EWMA Z-scores) alongside unconditional NASA-STD-3001 and ACC/AHA clinical safety thresholds. If a vital enters a critical zone (e.g., BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or cabin CO2 ≥ 3000 ppm), the system overrides the drifting baseline and triggers an immediate safety alert. A blind-spot-aware fusion engine visibly reduces confidence scores if sensors disconnect.

- Predict (Multi-Horizon Forecasting): Uses linear regression and Monte Carlo uncertainty modeling to project physiological trajectories 48 hours to 30 days ahead, uncovering sub-clinical risks before symptoms manifest.

- Act (Astronaut-Centric Guidance): Non-physician crews interact with a 9-organ clickable vector human body featuring a "Hazard Lens" filter, and follow branching clinical decision-tree wizards categorized into 4 escalation tiers: Tier 1 (Self-Manage), Tier 2 (Monitor), Tier 3 (Contact Flight Surgeon), and Tier 4 (Emergency Protocol). Includes an onboard ultrasound scanner with touch canvas annotation and an adherence gamification system.

- Learn (Self-Calibrating N-of-1 Trials): Evaluates countermeasure efficacy post-intervention by measuring Z-score delta (ΔZ), classifying treatments as PROMISING, INCONCLUSIVE, or INEFFECTIVE to continuously tune personalized care.

2. Benefits & Creative Innovations

- Solves Baseline Drift: Unlike conventional fitness trackers that mistake chronic pathology for a "new normal," our dual-layer safety engine guarantees absolute clinical safety boundaries.

- Non-Physician UX: Translates complex aerospace medicine into an intuitive clickable vector anatomy and step-by-step diagnostic decision trees.

- Multi-Environment Mode: Dynamically recalculates hazard risk formulas across 5 mission regimes: Deep Space Spacecraft (0g), Space Station (0g), Lunar Surface Base (0.16g), Mars Surface Base (0.38g), and Planetary Rover, strictly normalizing hazard weights to 1.0000.

- Overexertion Safety Guard: The habit gamification engine automatically pauses XP rewards if an astronaut's heart rate or fatigue indicates overexertion.

3. Intended Impact

Humanity's journey to Mars involves one-way communication latencies of up to 22 minutes (44+ minutes round trip), making real-time telemedicine from Earth impossible. ASTRA-LOOP provides total onboard medical autonomy, enabling crews to assess, predict, and treat their own health conditions without cloud dependency. Beyond spaceflight, ASTRA-LOOP’s offline architecture has direct terrestrial applications for remote clinical environments on Earth, including Antarctic research stations, naval submarines, and underserved rural communities.

4. Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Frontend: Next.js 14 (App Router), React, Tailwind CSS, Lucide Icons, Recharts data visualization. Optimized for desktop and responsive mobile screens (390px).

- Backend & Math Engines: Node.js, Express, TypeScript (strict mode), and Zod schema validation.

- Database & Storage: Prisma ORM with self-contained, zero-configuration SQLite (dev.db) for 100% offline edge execution, paired with browser IndexedDB for Delay-Tolerant Networking (DTN) queuing.

- Live Data Ingestion: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) live GOES-16/18 solar proton flux API with bundled offline cached fallback.

- Testing & Quality: Vitest test suite with 34 automated unit and integration tests passing. Containerized via Docker & Docker Compose.

5. Critical Factors Considered by Our Team

- Communication Delay: Designed from day one to run 100% offline inside the spacecraft habitat with zero cloud reliance.

- Non-Physician Cognitive Load: Created high-contrast, accessible UI (WCAG AA compliant) that avoids color-only status indicators, ensuring high usability under stress.

- Synergistic Space Hazards: Integrated interaction terms into our risk formulas to model how co-occurring hazards (e.g., severe sleep debt combined with solar radiation storms) amplify physiological damage exponentially.

- Medical Honesty: Transparently architected as an educational decision-support prototype rather than an FDA-certified diagnostic device, visibly labeling all synthetic demonstration data.
